Per the April 11, 2023 patch, Guardian Angel has a 1.5 s cooldown. If you slingshot with a Jump or Crouch cancel, the cooldown doesn't start until the extended flight ends. That flight lasts 1.5 s and can't be cancelled early, so you wait about 3 s in total (1.5 s of boosted flight plus the 1.5 s cooldown) before using it again.

The Mercy page says the extension lasts 1 second, but that is the pre-patch value, since the patch raised it from 1.0 to 1.5 s. The passages don't cover any changes after April 2023, so I can't say whether these numbers still hold today.

**Without Amp It Up:** Crossfade's Speed Boost gives **25%** movement speed (raised from 20% in the October 15, 2019 patch).

**With Amp It Up:** The passages only say the boost is **amplified by 60%** (raised from 50% in the same patch). They don't state the final figure. If the amplification multiplies the base boost, that works out to about 25% × 1.6 = **40%**, but that is my calculation, not a number from the passages.

The passages list no later changes to these values, so these are the latest figures they contain.

In Overwatch, **hitscan** describes a weapon or ability that has **no travel time**: the moment it fires, it hits whatever is under the shooter's crosshairs. There is no projectile to lead or dodge.

- **Examples:** Cassidy's Peacekeeper and Widowmaker's Widow's Kiss.
- **Contrast with projectiles:** A projectile weapon, such as Pharah's Rocket Launcher or Reinhardt's Fire Strike, takes time to travel and only hits if it physically collides with the target.
- **Damage falloff:** Hitscan weapons are subject to falloff, so they deal less damage at long range (typically about 30% at max range). Ana's scoped shots are an exception.
- **Subtypes:** Pinpoint (perfectly accurate, e.g. Ashe's ADS), spread (becomes erratic as you keep firing, e.g. Tracer), and recoil (the weapon climbs upward, e.g. Soldier: 76).

This is also why hitscan heroes are considered a major threat to Echo, who spends a lot of time in the air.

**Circuit Royal** is the map set in Monaco (specifically Monte Carlo). It's an Escort map in Overwatch 2, released on 26 April 2022 as the 35th map added to the game (the release-date list also shows it as entry 39 in its own numbering, but the map page itself says 35th). It takes place around the Monte Carlo casino front, a vertical curving racetrack, and the hotel.

Per the passages, Guardian Angel's cooldown is **1.5 seconds**, and it starts when the ability's duration ends (Passage 1).

History in the passages:
- **April 5, 2016:** Cooldown was reduced from 2 to 1.5 seconds.
- **July 19, 2016:** Guardian Angel instantly resets when Resurrect is used.
- **April 11, 2023:** Cooldown was reduced from 2.5 to 1.5 seconds. The Jump/Crouch cancel state was lengthened from 1.0 to 1.5 seconds, and it can no longer be manually interrupted to start the cooldown early. This effectively adds an extra 1.5 seconds if you use the cancel option.

Passage 1 says the Jump/Crouch extension lasts 1 second, but the April 2023 patch raised it to 1.5 seconds. That page may be out of date on this detail. The passages don't show any later changes to the cooldown.

The passages don't give a separate cooldown for Flash Heal with Double Dose, so it appears unchanged at **12 seconds**.

- The 14 Apr 2026 patch made Flash Heal a baseline ability and reduced its cooldown from 15 to 12 seconds.
- The Double Dose major perk only adds a charge and reduces Flash Heal's base healing by 10, from 60 to 50. It lists no cooldown change.

The passages don't say how the cooldown works across the two charges, for example whether they recharge one at a time. I can't confirm that from them.

Stadium has a different "Double Dose" Power that adds a charge and refreshes one when Valkyrie is activated. The passages don't give a Flash Heal cooldown for Stadium.

**In standard 5v5 Overwatch, Sleep Dart lasts up to 3 seconds against Tank heroes.** The July 9, 2024 patch cut it from 3.5 to 3 seconds. It had previously been cut from 5 to 3.5 seconds on April 11, 2023.

Other modes differ:
- **6v6:** Since December 17, 2024, Sleep Dart no longer has a reduced duration against Tanks, so they sleep as long as other heroes. The passages imply that is 5 seconds, but they don't state it outright for 6v6.
- **Stadium:** The Comfy Cloud power text lists the tank duration as 3.5 seconds, or 1.75 seconds with that power.

The passages don't explicitly name a "signature ability" for Mercy, so I can't say for certain which one is officially labeled that way.

The closest they come is the developer comment in Patch 1.15, which calls resurrecting downed allies "a core part of Mercy's gameplay" and says Resurrect is "an important part of Mercy's kit." Resurrect was originally her Ultimate (Q). Since the 19 Sep 2017 change it has been a single-target ability with a 30-second cooldown, and Valkyrie became her Ultimate.

The passages also list her other abilities, including the Caduceus Staff (healing and damage boost), Caduceus Blaster, Guardian Angel and Valkyrie. Resurrect is the one the developers single out as central to her identity.

The passages point to **Odessa "Dez" Stone, the Junker Queen**. She is listed as the current ruler of Junkertown, having replaced the banished King Mason Howl.

She started as a gladiator champion in the Scrapyard. She was the first Wastelander to reach the Reckoning's grand final, where she faced Howl, Geiger and Meri. Her infobox lists "Gladiator champion" as a *former* occupation, so she is now the ruler rather than an active arena champion. The passages don't say how the final ended, only that she is the current ruler.

Roadhog's Chain Hook cooldown is currently **6 seconds** in 5v5 and **7 seconds** in 6v6. The October 6, 2026 patch lowered it from 7 to 6 seconds in 5v5 and from 8 to 7 in 6v6.

The cooldown starts when the ability ends, not when it starts. That has been the case since the March 7, 2023 patch.

Anran's younger brother is **Wuyang Ye**. He is three years younger than her. He didn't pass the exam for the Fire College and ended up in Wuxing University's Water College. Anran is very protective of him, and both were recruited to Overwatch at the same time.

- The Chain Boost major perk adds another 5%, for 30% with the perk, and it also links to a second ally.
- The Mercy page's perk section still lists "+30% dealt", which looks like the old value or the Chain Boost value and hasn't been updated.

Sigma's real name is **Siebren de Kuiper**. He is a Dutch astrophysicist (formerly based in The Hague) who was turned into a living weapon for Talon. "Sigma" is his hero name.

Sigma's melee-enhancing major perk is **Hyper Strike**.

Every 5 direct hits with Hyperspheres, your next successful Quick Melee levitates and knocks away enemies. It deals 50 damage over 0.37 seconds on top of the base quick melee's 40 damage, for 90 total.

His other major perk, Levitation, is a movement perk and doesn't affect melee.

Winston comes from the **Horizon Lunar Colony**, a moon base established by Lucheng Interstellar. He is a genetically enhanced gorilla who was part of an experiment on the effects of prolonged habitation in space. Dr. Harold Winston took him under his wing and taught him science.

After the other gorillas staged an uprising and killed the scientists, he took Dr. Winston's name, built a makeshift rocket and escaped to Earth. He then joined Overwatch, and his base of operations is now Watchpoint: Gibraltar.

Mercy's Flash Heal cooldown is currently **12 seconds** in standard Overwatch (PvP).

History from the passages:
- **18 Feb 2025:** Flash Heal introduced as a perk (a Resurrect-linked ability) with a 15-second cooldown.
- **22 Apr 2025:** Flash Heal and Resurrect were decoupled, and it kept a 15-second cooldown as a Major Perk.
- **14 Apr 2026:** Flash Heal moved to Mercy's baseline kit, with the cooldown reduced from 15 to 12 seconds (base healing 50 → 60, multiplier on low-health allies 3x → 2x).

Related: the Double Dose major perk gives Flash Heal an additional charge but reduces its base healing by 10.

The passages don't list a Flash Heal cooldown for Stadium mode. There, the changes only mention Powers and Items that interact with it (for example, Double Dose refreshes a charge when Valkyrie is activated).

Winston's shield ability is **Barrier Projector** (called "Barrier Projection" in early patch notes). It creates a protective dome that covers him and nearby allies. The passages note that it covers him in a 360-degree radius, unlike Reinhardt's Barrier Field. It was reduced from 1000 to 600 shield health in the March 1, 2016 patch.

In Overwatch community slang, **"C9"** means losing a round by leaving or ignoring the objective during overtime, even though your team had the advantage (for example, after winning the team fight and getting key eliminations). It's also sometimes used for any case where a team fails to touch the point.

The term comes from the pro team **Cloud9**, which made this mistake multiple times in a tournament match. According to the passages, this happened in Overwatch APEX Season 2 in early 2017, against Afreeca Freecs Blue, on Lijiang Tower and Volskaya Industries.
The head of the Hashimoto clan is **Shion**, listed as the "head elder." The other elders are Seira Horvath, Kohaku Ogata, Tsubaki Serizawa, and Yaemon Ijuuin.

Cole Cassidy's old in-game name was **McCree** (Jesse McCree). The developers named him after a Blizzard developer, Jesse McCree. After that developer was fired in 2021 amid the California lawsuit against Activision Blizzard, the hero was renamed "Cole Cassidy". The change was announced in October 2021 and made permanent on October 26, 2021.
The Junker Queen's real name is **Odessa Stone** (alias "Dez"), and her nationality is **Australian**. She is the ruler of Junkertown, Australia.
Mercy (Angela Ziegler) is from **Switzerland**. Her base of operations was formerly Zürich, Switzerland, and she is now at Watchpoint: Gibraltar.

"C9" comes from the professional North American team **Cloud9**. During the Overwatch APEX Season 2 tournament in early 2017, Cloud9 played Afreeca Freecs Blue and lost multiple rounds, notably on Lijiang Tower and Volskaya Industries. They lost them by stepping off the objective during overtime, even though they had won the team fights and secured important eliminations.

As a term, "C9" now means losing a round by ignoring or stepping off the objective in overtime despite having the advantage.

In Overwatch, "Rez" (or "Revive") is a callout for a resurrection ability:

- Mercy's **Resurrect**
- Anran's **Vermillion Revival**

The passages also mention "Rez" as the name of a Russian streamer who organizes the Rez Community Cup (Rezcup). That is a name, not the gameplay term.
